text: You need the maximum sum of every window of `k` consecutive elements in an array of length `n`. Recomputing each window from scratch costs O(n*k). What does a sliding window cost?
An array has `n` elements. How many windows of exactly `k` consecutive elements does it contain (assume `k <= n`)?
When a fixed-size window slides one step to the right, how is the running window sum updated?
options: Recompute the sum of all `k` elements in the new window
Add the element that enters only
Add the element that enters and subtract the element that leaves
Subtract the element that enters and add the element that leaves
answer: Add the element that enters and subtract the element that leaves

text: In 'longest substring without repeating characters', when must the left edge of the window move right?
options: After every step of the right pointer
Only when the window length reaches `k`
When the character just added has never been seen before
When the character just added already appears in the window
answer: When the character just added already appears in the window

text: Which of these problems uses a fixed-size window rather than a variable-size one?
options: Maximum sum of any 3 consecutive elements
Shortest subarray with sum at least `target`
Longest subarray with at most 2 distinct values
answer: Maximum sum of any 3 consecutive elements

text: To find the maximum number of vowels in any substring of length `k`, what should the window keep track of?

How many vowels are currently inside the window
The index of the most recent vowel
A sorted list of the characters in the window

text: In a variable-size window where `left` and `right` only move forward, how many times is each element added to and removed from the window?

Added and removed about log n times
Added once and removed at most once
Added once, but removed up to `n` times

text: For 'shortest subarray with sum at least `target`', why is it safe to shrink the window from the left once the sum reaches `target`?
options: The array is sorted, so the smallest element is always on the left
All numbers are positive, so removing an element from the left can only lower the sum
The target is always reached exactly once
Each subarray is checked twice, so nothing can be missed
answer: All numbers are positive, so removing an element from the left can only lower the sum

text: In 'shortest subarray with sum at least `target`', when should the best length be updated?
options: After the shrink loop finishes, when the sum has dropped below `target`
Only once `right` reaches the end of the array
Inside the shrink loop, while the sum is still at least `target`, before `nums[left]` is removed
Before `nums[right]` is added to the sum
answer: Inside the shrink loop, while the sum is still at least `target`, before `nums[left]` is removed

text: Why does a variable-size window usually shrink with `while` rather than `if`?
options: Using `if` would make the algorithm O(n^2)
Adding one element can require removing several elements from the left before the window is valid again
The `while` loop is what moves the right pointer
There is no difference; `if` and `while` always behave the same here
answer: Adding one element can require removing several elements from the left before the window is valid again

text: In 'at most `k` distinct characters', when a character's count drops to `0` while shrinking, what must you do?

    count, left, total = {}, 0, 0
    for right, x in enumerate(nums):

            if count[nums[left]] == 0:

            left += 1
        total += right - left + 1
